Below is a **complete, minimal, and ready‑to‑run** Rust application that

1. Reads the current clipboard text (Windows, macOS, Linux – any platform that supports the clipboard).
2. Sends that text to the ElevenLabs TTS API.
3. Streams the returned MP3 audio to your speakers.

> **Why ElevenLabs?**  
> ElevenLabs offers a very natural‑sounding TTS engine. The API is simple: you POST a JSON payload with the text and a voice ID, and you get back an MP3 blob.  
> The example below uses the *“eleven_monolingual_v1”* voice (the default). If you want a different voice, replace the `voice_id` string with the ID you get from the ElevenLabs dashboard.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | How to get it |
|------|---------------|
| **Rust** | Install from <https://rustup.rs/> |
| **ElevenLabs API key** | Sign up at <https://elevenlabs.io>, go to *API* → *API Key* |
| **A voice ID** | In the ElevenLabs dashboard, click *Voice Library* → *Create new voice* (or use the default “eleven_monolingual_v1”). |
| **Audio output** | Any system with a working sound card. |

> **Tip** – Store your API key in an environment variable so it never ends up in source control:

```bash
# Linux/macOS
export ELEVENLABS_API_KEY="YOUR_KEY_HERE"

# Windows (PowerShell)
$env:ELEVENLABS_API_KEY="YOUR_KEY_HERE"
```

---

```bash
cargo new elevenlabs_clipboard_tts
cd elevenlabs_clipboard_tts
```

Below is a **complete, end‑to‑end recipe** for building a tiny “dummy‑data” web app with:

| Layer | Tech | What it does |
|-------|------|--------------|
| **Backend** | Node.js + Express | REST API that stores a list of items in memory (you can swap it for MongoDB, Postgres, etc.) |
| **Frontend** | React (Create‑React‑App) | UI that lets you add an item and lists all items |
| **Deployment** | Heroku (backend) + Netlify (frontend) | One of the simplest free‑tier options.  (I’ll also show how to do it with Docker or Render if you prefer.) |

> **Why this stack?**  
> *Node/Express* is the most common “JavaScript on the server” choice.  
> *React* is the de‑facto UI library.  
> *Heroku + Netlify* let you deploy with a single command and no server‑side configuration.
